picker_law_generic_catalog_class_archite.note: Closes the picker_law question for the entire CATALOG-2 generic-CRUD catalog class (GenericCatalogPage.tsx + CatalogEditModal.tsx + GENERIC_CATALOG_REGISTRY in useCatalogQuery.ts, 83 registry entries spanning accounting/customers/dispatch/driver/fleet/fuel/maintenance/safety/vendors), not just individual catalogs. Proof, not a spot-guess: (1) CatalogFieldType (useCatalogQuery.ts:4) declares 'foreign_key' as a supported type — the picker capability exists (CatalogEditModal.tsx renders a real Combobox for it, fixed this session, PR #13599) — but `grep -c foreign_key` on the 83-entry registry returns exactly 1 hit, the type-union declaration itself; zero of the 83 entries assign it. (2) 3 fresh live spot-checks this session across independent domains — accounting.account_role_bindings (0 rows, no page-level Create button exists at all), maintenance.maintenance_vendors (5 rows, Code/Display Name/Description/Order/Status, no FK), fuel.fuel_stations (0 rows, Create modal = Code/Fuel Station/Description/Sort Order, no FK) — all match the uniform flat shape. Cross-catalog references that ARE genuinely picked (vendor, account, class, payment_term, load_trailer_equipment, etc.) route through the SEPARATE catalogPickerRegistry.ts (42 keys) consumed by ReferenceSelect elsewhere in the app, not through the generic catalog's own create/edit form — verify-lst-picker01-consumer-adoption (verify-step 2358) PASSES against all 42. Net: a generic-catalog leaf's OWN create/edit modal is correctly zero-picker by architecture; picker_law for these leaves is satisfied by their registry consumer wiring, not by anything inside GenericCatalogPage/CatalogEditModal. Documents an acceptable non-gap at the class level so future sweeps don't re-open already-closed leaves one at a time.
